summary.en-US: Open any page or link in its own throwaway container: no cookies, no logins, nothing carried over. The container is deleted when you close the tab.

description.en-US:
Isolate gives each isolated tab its own brand-new Firefox container, so it starts with no cookies, no logins and no site storage from your other tabs or earlier sessions. When the last tab in a container closes, its cookies, local storage, IndexedDB and service workers are wiped and the container is deleted.

How to use:
- Click the toolbar button (or press Ctrl+Alt+I) to reopen the current page in a new isolated tab.
- Right-click a link and choose "Open Link in Isolated Tab".
- Isolated tabs show an ISO badge on the toolbar button.

Isolated tabs also block Google "Sign in with Google" One Tap prompts.

Notes:
- Desktop Firefox only. Containers are not available in private windows, so isolated tabs open in a normal window.
- Isolate collects no data and makes no network requests of its own.

Source code: https://github.com/shad0wcrawl3r/isolate

version.approval_notes: No build step; the submitted files are the source. Permissions: contextualIdentities/cookies to create a fresh container per isolated tab; browsingData to wipe a container's data when its last tab closes; webRequest/webRequestBlocking with <all_urls> to cancel accounts.google.com/gsi requests inside isolated containers only, and to register a CSS-only content script (suppress.css) scoped to those containers; contextMenus for the link menu item; storage to remember which containers to clean up after a restart.
